statement: Median per-capita disposable income growth < mean growth in 2027 annual data (national statistics offices; one indicator per leading jurisdiction)
status_at_phase_end: Not resolvable in 2023. Bloc B: in the 2022 annual data (published Jan 2023) median growth (4.7%) was below mean growth (5.0%), and in Q1-Q3 2023 data median growth (5.4%) was again below mean (6.3%) - the YES pattern held in-phase. Full-year 2023 data (published Jan 2024) excluded. Bloc A: no per-capita disposable median/mean series; the closest official release (money income, 2022) showed real median household income -2.3% while the Gini index fell, a mixed signal for the median-vs-mean test.

items.summary: Bloc B statistics office, 2022 annual: per-capita disposable income 36,883 yuan, +5.0% nominal; median 31,370 yuan, +4.7% (85.1% of mean) - median growth below mean growth.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS 'Households' Income and Consumption Expenditure in 2022', released 2023-01-17 (NBS English page blocked to fetcher; verified via the NBS text republished on govt.chinadaily.com.cn, dated 2023-01-18, via web_extract this run).

items.summary: Bloc B statistics office, first three quarters of 2023: per-capita disposable income 29,398 yuan, +6.3% nominal; median 24,528 yuan, +5.4% (83.4% of mean) - median growth below mean growth.
items.detail: Bloc B NBS 'Households' Income and Consumption Expenditure in the First Three Quarters of 2023', 2023-10-19 (headline figures in NBS release of 2023-10-18) (verified via web_extract this run). Urban median +4.3% vs urban mean +5.2%; rural median +5.7% vs rural mean +7.6%.

items.summary: Bloc A statistics office, 2022 money income: real median household income fell 2.3% to $74,580; the money-income Gini index fell from 0.494 to 0.488 (the release flags this as a notable first decline). Not a per-capita disposable median-vs-mean series.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau press release CB23-150, 'Income, Poverty and Health Insurance Coverage in the Bloc A: 2022', 2023-09-12 (verified via web_extract this run). A falling Gini suggests the mean did not outpace the median in 2022, but the series concept (household money income, pre-tax) differs from the indicator.
